papers.title_en: Standing on the Shoulders of Giants: Enhancing LLM Agents for Automated Fact-Checking with Human Expert Skills
papers.authors: Xinwen Chen, Haorui He, Yupeng Li
papers.evidence: 基于LLM智能体的证据检索与论断验证自动事实核查
papers.tldr: LLM智能体自动事实核查在证据检索与验证上受限于高成本后训练或难扩展人工反馈。作者将AFP Fact Check指南蒸馏为模块化技能PFC-Skill，并提出SkillCheck在推理时动态调用以指导检索与验证。在AVeriTeC，较DEFAME基线准确率提升2.2–4.8个百分点、Macro-F1 1.5–6.3个百分点；GPT-4o-Mini准确率超GPT-4o版3.4个百分点且推理成本降61%。消融显示检索阶段贡献最大，两阶段最佳。
papers.abstract_en: Automated fact-checking (AFC) systems powered by large language model (LLM) agents still face challenges in evidence retrieval and claim verification. Existing approaches improve their capabilities through computationally costly post-training or human-in-the-loop feedback that is difficult to scale. To transfer professional fact-checking expertise to LLM agents efficiently, we distill publicly available guidelines published by Agence France-Presse (AFP) Fact Check into a reusable, modular Professional Fact-Checking Skill (PFC-Skill). We then present SkillCheck, the first AFC system that gives LLM agents dynamic access to PFC-Skill to guide evidence retrieval and claim verification at inference time. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SkillCheck improves upon skill-free DEFAME baselines across multiple LLM backbones, with gains of 2.2--4.8 pp. in Accuracy and 1.5--6.3 pp. in Macro-F1 on the AVeriTeC benchmark. Notably, SkillCheck with GPT-4o-Mini exceeds DEFAME with GPT-4o by 3.4 pp. in Accuracy while cutting inference cost by roughly 61%. The performance gains also extend to open-web retrieval. Ablations show that incorporating the skill during evidence retrieval provides most of the gains, while incorporation into both stages yields the best overall performance. Case studies show that PFC-Skill enables more targeted search and closer scrutiny of evidence. To conclude, our work shows that LLM agents can "stand on the shoulders of giants" by drawing on the best practices of professional fact-checkers, substantially enhancing AFC performance without extra training or continuous human supervision.

papers.title_en: MemeLogos: Knowledge-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Harmful Meme Detection
papers.authors: Hexiang Gu, Saihui Hou, Changlan Liu, Min Ren, Huijia Wu, Hongxun Gu, Zhaofeng He
papers.evidence: 面向有害模因检测的知识驱动检索增强多模态推理
papers.tldr: 社交媒体中有害模因的危害常隐含在图文与语境交互中，现有检索增强方法难捕捉可复用知识与推理机制。MemeLogos将反复出现的有害模式与推理结构抽象为知识单元，构建星形知识图谱，并结合结构化检索与多阶段显式推理。实验表明其检测性能稳定优于现有方法，推理更连贯可解释。该工作验证了结构化危害知识对多模态内容理解的价值。
papers.abstract_en: With the rapid proliferation of social media, harmful memes have become a growing threat to online ecosystems. Their harmfulness is often implicitly conveyed through complex interactions among visual, textual, and contextual cues, making accurate detection challenging. Recent studies have introduced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and external knowledge into harmful meme detection. However, existing methods mainly retrieve similar instances or auxiliary information, limiting their ability to capture reusable harmfulness knowledge and underlying reasoning mechanisms, and thus constraining both detection performance and interpretability. To address these challenges, we propose MemeLogos, a knowledge-driven retrieval-augmented reasoning framework for harmful meme detection. MemeLogos abstracts recurring harmfulness patterns and reasoning structures from diverse harmful cases into reusable knowledge units and organizes them into a dedicated star-shaped knowledge graph. By combining structured knowledge retrieval with an explicit multi-stage reasoning process inspired by cognitive mechanisms, MemeLogos leverages retrieved knowledge to guide harmfulness reasoning, improving both detection reliability and interpretability. Extensive experiments show that MemeLogos consistently outperforms existing harmful meme detection methods while generating more coherent and interpretable reasoning, demonstrating the effectiveness of structured harmfulness knowledge for multimodal content understanding.

papers.title_en: VisualTrust: Video Reasoning under On-Screen Claim Framing
papers.authors: Huachao Zhu, Junjielong Xu, Sicheng Li, Liang Yang, Mingtao Chen, Zhichao Hu, Li Jiang, Pinjia He
papers.evidence: 研究误导性屏幕文字与视频画面证据冲突时的判定
papers.tldr: 屏幕文字既能描述视频，也能框定其含义，模型可能让文字声称压过冲突的视觉证据。作者提出反事实基准 VisualTrust，以无声称、准确声称和误导声称三版视频检验声称顺从，并设计免训练框架 DEAR，分离证据仲裁与阅读。误导声称使平均准确率从90.1%降至51.9%，42.8%的初始正确回答转向陷阱。DEAR将误导下准确率提至81.8–85.2%，陷阱选择降至11.6–15.0%，同时保持无声称准确率。
papers.abstract_en: On-screen text can describe what a video shows, or it can frame what the video is supposed to mean. Current benchmarks treat both alike, testing whether a model can read the text rather than whether it should trust it. We study claim deference, multimodal large language models' tendency to let an on-screen claim override conflicting visual evidence. We introduce VisualTrust, a counterfactual benchmark with 5,063 cases across 14 claim-fact classes. Each case pairs a question with three versions of the same video: one with no claim, one with an accurate claim, and one with a misleading claim that alters a single grounded fact. The option the misleading claim supports is the trap answer. Across seven open-weight and four proprietary models, mean accuracy falls from 90.1% without a claim to 51.9% with a misleading claim. Among initially correct responses, 42.8% flip to the trap answer and only 0.6% become other errors. Strong no-claim accuracy does not ensure resistance. We also introduce DEAR (Decoupled Evidence Arbitration and Reading), a training-free agent for video question answering that separates evidence arbitration from reading. An independent check reports conflicting evidence, a selector weighs it without a fixed modality priority and blinds what it withholds, and the reader answers from the resulting video in a fresh context. On 500 videos across three proprietary models, DEAR raises accuracy under misleading claims from 47.2--64.0% to 81.8--85.2% and reduces trap-answer selection from 34.4--50.8% to 11.6--15.0%, while preserving no-claim accuracy.

papers.title_en: Media Intelligence Platform: Multimodal Detection of Synthetic and Manipulated Content
papers.authors: David Fischinger, Marcel Hasenbalg, Silvia Poletti, Davide Antonutti, Mina Schütz, Lam Pham, Justin Ilyes, Péter Rjabcsenkó, Simon Freitter, Martin Boyer
papers.evidence: 统一检测合成与篡改图像、视频、音频与文本的多模态框架
papers.tldr: 生成式AI使合成人脸、伪造视频、AI图像、假音频与局部篡改图像大量涌现，但现有检测方法多只针对单一篡改类型，难以应对真实场景中的异构媒体。作者提出基于Web的媒体情报平台MIP，以模块化架构统一集成假视频、人脸变形、AI生成图像、音频深度伪造、局部图像篡改与文本分析等专用检测模块。在代表性基准数据集上的实验表明，各模态均取得可靠检测性能，并提供面向取证调查的易用界面。该工作展示了统一多模态取证系统的可行性，并发布公开演示以支持复现与社区评测。
papers.abstract_en: The rapid progress of generative artificial intelligence has led to a significant increase in manipulated multimedia content, including synthetic faces, forged videos, AI-generated images, fake audio, and locally edited images. Existing detection approaches are typically designed for a single manipulation type, limiting their applicability in real-world scenarios involving heterogeneous media sources. In this work, we present the Media Intelligence Platform (MIP), a unified web-based framework for multimodal media forensics integrating specialized modules for fake video detection, face morphing detection, AI-generated image detection, audio deepfake detection, localized image manipulation detection, and text analysis. Its modular architecture enables flexible integration of heterogeneous models and supports future extensions for emerging manipulation techniques. Experimental results on representative benchmark datasets demonstrate reliable detection performance across multiple media modalities while providing a practical and user-friendly interface for forensic investigations. The platform highlights the potential of unified multimodal systems for comprehensive deepfake detection in real-world environments, and is accompanied by a public demonstrator released with this workshop submission to support reproducibility and community evaluation.

papers.title_en: Leveraging LLM-Generated Explanations for Detecting Emotionally Rewritten Fake News
papers.authors: Yupei Guo, Jiajun He, Xiaohan Shi, Tomoki Toda, Zekun Yang, Bowen Wang, Yukinobu Taniguchi
papers.evidence: 大模型生成解释提升虚假新闻检测鲁棒性
papers.tldr: 假新闻检测常受事实不变但情绪化改写的影响，现有模型对这类改写不够稳健。作者构建情绪改写测试集，并用LLM从原文生成解释作为稳定背景知识，提出门控交叉注意力GCA自适应融合新闻与解释。在PolitiFact、LUN多种情绪条件下显著提升，GossipCop保持竞争性。该工作为事实保持型情绪改写场景下的鲁棒假新闻检测提供了新的测试数据和可解释融合框架。
papers.abstract_en: The spread of fake news may cause severe social consequences. Existing fake news detection methods mainly focus on stylistic variations or incorporate external information such as explanations. However, news articles are often rewritten under different emotional backgrounds while preserving their underlying factual claims, which may affect the robustness of detection models. In this work, we investigate fake news detec- tion under fact-preserving emotional variations. To study this problem, we construct emotion-rewritten test sets and generate explanations from the original news articles as stable background knowledge. We then propose a Gated Cross Attention (GCA) framework that adaptively integrates emotionally rewritten news with the corresponding explanations, enabling the model to focus on informative explanation content while reducing potential mismatches caused by emotional reframing. Experiments on PolitiFact, GossipCop, and LUN demonstrate that the proposed method achieves notable improvements under multiple emotional conditions on PolitiFact and LUN, while maintaining competitive performance on GossipCop. We further analyze the effects of explanation guidance and gating mechanisms under different emotional conditions. Our code and data are available at: https://github.com/Flulike/fakenews gca .

papers.title_en: UkrMeme: Multimodal Explainable Persuasion Detection in Ukrainian Memes
papers.authors: Nazar Andrushko, Vera Schmitt, Veronika Solopova
papers.evidence: 用视觉语言模型可解释地检测模因说服手法
papers.tldr: 乌克兰战时模因常以图文组合传递说服信息，但缺乏标注资源与可解释检测基准。作者构建UkrMeme（200条有机模因）和PTM-UA（Propaganda 950子集乌译），在零样本提示下用VLMs处理图像、文本与多模态输入，并以层级F1评估。研究比较LRP与模型生成token归因，分析两类解释强调的证据语义类别。该工作为乌克兰语多模态说服检测与解释性评估提供数据和方法基础。
papers.abstract_en: Memes play a central role in modern online communication, especially in contexts of political conflict where visual and textual cues combine to convey persuasive messages. We study persuasive technique detection in Ukrainian memes using vision-language models (VLMs). We introduce UkrMeme, a dataset of 200 organically produced Ukrainian wartime memes annotated for persuasion techniques, and PTM-UA, a Ukrainian translation of a subset of the Propaganda 950 benchmark that preserves original visual content while translating meme text. We evaluate VLMs in a zero-shot prompting setup across image, text, and multimodal inputs using hierarchical F1 metrics. Finally, we compare Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) and model-generated token attributions and analyze the semantic categories of evidence emphasized by each explanation method.

papers.title_en: EviStress: Evidence Stress Learning for Generalizable Face Forgery Detection with Textual Explanations
papers.authors: Jiuyao Jing, Xuanyu Yi, Yu Zheng, Chunlei Peng
papers.evidence: 可泛化的视觉伪造检测与文本解释
papers.tldr: 网络人脸伪造持续演化且传播中经历多样处理，现有LoRA-CLIP检测器过度依赖少量高相关视觉patch，面对未知操纵和视觉变化不够可靠。EviStress采用两阶段框架：ETPP对高依赖patch进行证据压力扰动，DVP保留真伪判别信息；IEIT将适配CLIP接入LLaVA做指令微调。实验显示跨数据集、跨方法泛化和腐蚀鲁棒性提升，并能输出真实性预测与文本解释。
papers.abstract_en: The rapid spread of face forgeries on the Web challenges the credibility of visual content. In practical Web environments, manipulated media originate from evolving generation pipelines and undergo diverse processing during dissemination, making reliable authenticity assessment under unseen manipulations and visual changes a critical challenge. We observe that a standard LoRA-adapted CLIP detector exhibits uneven patch-level decision dependence, concen trating a disproportionate share of class-specific relevance on a small fraction of visual patches. To improve robustness to variations in such highly dependent evidence, we propose EviStress, a two-stage framework for generalizable face forgery detection with textual explanations. In the first stage, Evidence-Targeted Patch Perturbation (ETPP) estimates patch dependence from global, relational, and semantic cues and assigns positively correlated perturbation probabilities, explicitly stress-testing highly dependent visual evidence during training. We further introduce Discriminative Variation Preservation (DVP), which constrains the residual between clean and perturbed representations to retain authenticity discriminative information. In the second stage, Intrinsic Evidence Instruction Tuning (IEIT) transfers the adapted CLIP encoder into LLaVA as its vision tower and performs parameter-efficient multimodal instruction tuning, enabling authenticity prediction and textual explanation directly from the learned forgery-sensitive representation without an external detector. Experiments demonstrate improved cross-dataset and cross-method generalization and corruption robustness, with the multimodal model providing authenticity predictions and human-readable explanations.

papers.title_en: MemeTrace: A Multimodal LLM-Based Agent for Safety-Aware Meme Provenance Analysis
papers.authors: Bo Shao, Yihan Ma, Yiting Qu, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang
papers.evidence: 追踪承载虚假信息的模因的多模态大模型智能体
papers.tldr: 在线梗图常传播虚假信息与宣传等不安全内容，且演化快、依赖语境，现有审核多只对单图做安全二分类，缺少来源与风险溯源能力。为此，作者提出 MemeTrace，一个基于多模态大模型的安全感知梗图溯源智能体，可自动追踪新梗图的来源、传播脉络与潜在风险。在包含100个真实梗图的 Meme100 上，结合人工标注与自动指标评估，MemeTrace 明显优于 VLM 基线，对虚假信息和敏感内容等不安全梗图识别更准，并在视觉扰动下保持稳健。该工作把梗图审核从单图分类推进到溯源分析，为平台安全治理提供新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Online memes are often carriers of unsafe content such as disinformation and propaganda. Their rapid evolution in response to news events and strong dependence on contextual information make it difficult for platforms and moderators to detect and moderate them effectively. Moreover, existing moderation studies typically classify memes as safe or unsafe based on individual images, lacking the ability to perform broader provenance analysis, i.e., where a meme originates, how it spreads, what cultural symbolism it represents, whether it poses potential risks to society, etc. To bridge this gap, we introduce MemeTrace, a multimodal LLM-based agent that automatically traces the provenance and potential risks of emerging memes. We evaluate MemeTrace on Meme100, a dataset of 100 real-world memes, using both human annotation and automatic metrics. The results demonstrate that MemeTrace substantially outperforms the VLM baseline. More importantly, MemeTrace achieves higher accuracy in detecting unsafe memes, especially those involving disinformation and sensitive content, and remains robust under visual perturbations.

papers.title_en: Flow-CLIP: Image-Conditioned Residual Scoring for CompositionalImage-Text Matching
papers.authors: Minghong Wei, Enguang Zhu, Pu Cao, Lu Yang, Qing Song
papers.evidence: 基于词元与图块证据的细粒度图文组合匹配
papers.tldr: 组合式图文匹配要求模型区分对象、属性相同但绑定关系不同的描述，而现有 CLIP 的句子级全局对齐对此不足。Flow-CLIP 以图像条件化的 token–patch 局部证据变化校准全局相似度，并引入跨图像 margin 排序，让匹配图像支持正确描述时获得更大排名间隔。在组合匹配与属性–对象绑定基准上，该方法提升绑定准确率，并降低对语言先验的依赖。
papers.abstract_en: Vision--language pre-training has enabled substantial progress in image--text retrieval and zero-shot recognition by learning transferable cross-modal representations. However, sentence-level alignment remains insufficient for compositional matching, where captions can describe the same objects and attributes while differing in how these elements are bound. To address this limitation, we propose Flow-CLIP, which refines global image-text alignment through image-conditioned changes in token--patch evidence. Global Compatibility Calibration (GCC) learns a sentence-level similarity metric, while Image-Conditioned Evidence Refinement (ICER) incorporates visual patch context into token queries and uses the resulting change in local matching evidence to adjust the global score. We further introduce Cross-Image Margin Ranking (CIMR), which compares the same positive--negative caption pair across matched and mismatched images, encouraging a larger ranking margin when the image supports the correct description. Experiments on compositional matching and attribute--object binding benchmarks show that Flow-CLIP improves binding accuracy over pretrained CLIP and learned global alignment through local evidence refinement, while cross-image ranking supervision mitigates reliance on language priors. Code will be released at link.

papers.title_en: Can the Parts Fool the Test? Counterfactual Pairing Cycles for Relational OOD
papers.evidence: 反事实图文配对循环用于检测图文关系不匹配
papers.tldr: 关系型分布外评估常被图像统计、文本风格或长度等捷径污染，难以判断模型是否真的检查图文配对。作者提出反事实配对循环：固定两张图和两条描述，只交换配对方式，使单模态与加性捷径在有限样本中精确抵消，并可作为训练损失与双线性评分诊断。在合成控制、GQA和COCO上，该方法区分粗粒度匹配与方向性角色绑定失败，循环训练将CycleAcc从0.882提升到0.927。其意义在于把评测焦点从“部件是否合理”转向“配对耦合是否正确”。
papers.abstract_en: Relational out-of-distribution errors are easy to describe and hard to evaluate cleanly. An image may be natural, a caption may be fluent, and all mentioned objects may be common, yet the caption may describe the wrong relation in the image. Many evaluations intended to test this behavior can be solved without checking the pairing at all, because negatives differ in caption style, template, length, object frequency, or image statistics. We propose counterfactual pairing cycles, a blocked evaluation primitive that reuses the same two images and the same two captions on both sides of the comparison, changing only which image is paired with which caption. This makes image-only, text-only, and additive component shortcuts cancel exactly in finite samples. The same contrast also gives a training loss for relational outlier exposure and a diagnostic for bilinear vision-language scores. Across synthetic controls, GQA, and COCO, cycles separate coarse image-caption matching from directional role-binding failures, while also identifying geometric size relations that remain strongly visible in global features. In a shortcut-contaminated COCO outlier-exposure stress test, a model selected by a near-perfect shortcut validation AUROC retains substantial relational signal but remains below cycle training on exact cycles; cycle training improves CycleAcc from 0.882 to 0.927. The main lesson is simple: to test whether a model understands a pairing, the benchmark should keep the parts fixed, change the pairing, and ask only about coupling. The official implementation is available online.

papers.title_en: WildAIGC-Bench: Can AI Image Detectors Handle the Wild? A Benchmark of Generated and Edited Images in Online Circulation
papers.authors: Zijian Yu, Hangwei Zhang, Jun Lan, Huijia Zhu, Weiqiang Wang, Jianfu Zhang
papers.evidence: 在线传播中AI生成图像的基准与证据摘要
papers.tldr: AI生成或编辑图片在新闻与网络传播中易误导公众，现有检测基准难反映真实在线场景。WildAIGC-Bench通过持续采集新闻网站、事实核查与社交媒体内容，结合自动筛选和人工核验构建。其含407张经核验图片，保留压缩、截图、翻拍等在线条件；评测专用检测器、多模态大模型和感知编码器基线均显示明显召回差距。该基准为真实场景检测提供挑战，并支持后续数据扩展与来源核验。
papers.abstract_en: AI-generated images linked to news events and online claims can mislead audiences, enable fraud, or cause public controversy. We introduce WildAIGC-Bench, built through recurring collection across news websites, fact-checking sources, and related social media content. The pipeline combines broad coverage, timely updates, and human-verified labels through scheduled discovery, automatic screening and preliminary annotation, and human review of image-specific evidence. The benchmark contains 407 verified AI-generated or edited images, each accompanied by a source webpage link and an evidence summary. Images retain the conditions encountered online, including compression, screenshots, and recapture. Evaluation of dedicated visual detectors, multimodal large language models, and a simple Perception Encoder baseline reveals substantial recall gaps relative to existing benchmarks. WildAIGC-Bench provides both a practical detection challenge and a basis for continued data expansion and source-based verification. The dataset is released at https://github.com/YuZijian/WildAIGC-Bench.
